title: The Gifts of the Spirit
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The gifts of the Spirit are gracious abilities given by the Holy Spirit to believers for service, edification, order, and the glory of Christ. They are not given for pride, competition, or self-display.
summary: The gifts of the Spirit are gracious abilities given by the Holy Spirit to believers for service, edification, order, and the glory of Christ. They are not given for pride, competition, or self-display.
christFocus: The Spirit gives gifts so the body of Christ is built up and Christ is honored. Spiritual gifts are meant to serve the Lord’s people and advance His mission, not exalt the person who receives them.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Spiritual gifts come from the grace of God. The Spirit distributes gifts according to His will, and believers are called to use what they have received as stewards of God’s varied grace.

The purpose of the gifts is the building up of the church. Gifts are not spiritual trophies. They are given to serve, strengthen, teach, encourage, lead, help, and equip God’s people for faithful ministry.

The gifts must be governed by love and order. Scripture warns that visible gifts without love are empty. The Spirit does not give gifts to produce chaos, pride, or division, but edification and faithfulness.

Spiritual gifts also remind believers that every member matters. The body of Christ needs many kinds of service, including visible and hidden works of grace.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some believers become proud of visible gifts, while others feel useless because their service is quiet or overlooked. This doctrine corrects both errors by showing that all gifts come from grace and exist for service.

The church becomes unhealthy when gifts are used for platform, control, or comparison. The Spirit gives gifts so Christ’s body is strengthened in love and truth.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Use whatever grace God has given you to serve others. Do not bury your gift out of fear, and do not use it for pride. Seek love, faithfulness, humility, and the building up of the church. Measure usefulness by obedience to Christ, not applause.
